pages.caption: There was once upon a time a woman who lived in a small cottage.
pages.scene: A humble cottage in the countryside. The walls are rough stone and the roof is thatched with dry straw. Smoke rises from a small chimney.

pages.caption: The cottage was simple, warmed by a single hearth.
pages.scene: Inside the cottage. A hearth burns in the corner. A wooden table and two stools sit near the fire. Clay pots line the shelf.

pages.caption: She had a son called Minnikin.
pages.scene: The woman stands by the hearth. She is thin and worn from work. Her apron is patched and her hands are rough.

pages.caption: He was a brave boy, but very small for his age.
pages.scene: Minnikin stands in the doorway. He is very small for his age, but his shoulders are set and his chin is raised.

pages.caption: He was small, yet there was courage in his eyes.
pages.scene: Minnikin stands beside the table. He barely reaches the tabletop. His hands hang at his sides.

pages.caption: One day his mother said to him:
pages.scene: The mother turns from the hearth to face Minnikin. Her expression is serious and concerned.

pages.caption: Now, Minnikin, you are too little to be of any use.
pages.scene: Close on the mother's face. Her brow is furrowed. She looks down at her small son with worry.

pages.caption: Go out into the world and seek your fortune.
pages.scene: The mother gestures toward the open door. Beyond it the road winds out into rolling green hills under a wide sky.
pages.action: The mother points toward the door.

pages.caption: Minnikin heard his mother's words and knew what he must do.
pages.scene: Minnikin looks at the door, then back at his mother. The light from outside falls across his face.

pages.caption: He would not stay where he was of no use.
pages.scene: Minnikin crosses the cottage floor toward the door. His small footsteps leave no sound on the packed earth.

pages.caption: The world awaited beyond the cottage door.
pages.scene: Minnikin stands at the threshold. One foot is outside on the dirt path. His mother watches from the shadows.

pages.caption: So Minnikin set out.
pages.scene: Minnikin steps across the threshold. His small figure is framed against the bright daylight outside.

pages.caption: He walked along the road, small against the wide world.
pages.scene: The road stretches ahead through countryside. Wildflowers line the dirt path. The sky is wide and clear.

pages.caption: He had not gone far along the road.
pages.scene: Minnikin walks past a stone wall. A bird sits on top, watching him pass. His shadow stretches on the ground.

pages.caption: An old woman met him on the road.
pages.scene: An old woman appears ahead. She is hunched and wrapped in a dark shawl. Her face is deeply lined.

pages.caption: She asked him where he was going.
pages.scene: The old woman stops before Minnikin. She peers at him with dark, knowing eyes. Her staff is gnarled oak.

pages.caption: I am going to seek my fortune," said he.
pages.scene: Minnikin faces the old woman. He stands straight despite his height. The wind stirs the grass at his feet.

pages.caption: Then you may come with me," said the old woman.
pages.scene: The old woman smiles. Her wrinkled face creases deeper. She nods slowly.

pages.caption: She led him to a hidden place among the trees.
pages.scene: The old woman leads Minnikin off the road toward a thicket of trees. Branches arch overhead like a tunnel.
pages.action: The old woman leads Minnikin away from the road.

pages.caption: There stood a horse of extraordinary beauty.
pages.scene: In the clearing, a horse stands tied to a post. Its coat shines like silver. Its mane ripples in a breeze that touches nothing else.

pages.caption: I will give you a horse which can go as fast over land.
pages.scene: The old woman places her hand on the horse's neck. The animal does not flinch. It regards Minnikin with calm eyes.
pages.action: The old woman touches the horse.

pages.caption: As a ship goes over the sea," said the old woman.
pages.scene: The old woman turns to Minnikin. Her dark eyes are sharp and certain. The horse's coat catches the light.

pages.caption: Minnikin gazed upon the horse in wonder.
pages.scene: Minnikin looks at the horse, then at the old woman. Amazement shows on his young face.

pages.caption: Minnikin thanked her.
pages.scene: Minnikin bows his head. The old woman watches him with a satisfied expression.

pages.caption: He stepped toward the horse and reached for the reins.
pages.scene: Minnikin approaches the horse. He reaches up to touch its neck. The horse turns its head toward him.

pages.caption: And mounted the horse.
pages.scene: Minnikin puts one foot in the stirrup and swings himself onto the horse's back. The horse stands steady beneath him.

pages.caption: He sat upon the horse, ready to ride.
pages.scene: Minnikin sits astride the horse. The old woman stands below, looking up at him. The clearing is quiet.

pages.caption: And rode away.
pages.scene: The horse leaps forward. Minnikin grips the reins. The old woman shrinks behind them.

pages.caption: The horse flew along the road, faster than any animal Minnikin had known.
pages.scene: The horse carries Minnikin along the road at great speed. The trees blur past. The wind whips Minnikin's hair.

pages.caption: He rode on for some time.
pages.scene: The horse runs across open fields. The ground trembles under its hooves. Minnikin leans into the wind.
pages.action: The horse runs across the fields.

pages.caption: Then he came to a castle.
pages.scene: A castle appears in the distance. Its towers are tall and white against the blue sky. Banners fly from the highest turret.

pages.caption: The castle rose before him, tall and magnificent.
pages.scene: The horse carries Minnikin closer to the castle. The walls are high and made of pale stone. Windows glint in the sun.

pages.caption: The gates stood open, inviting him inside.
pages.scene: The castle gates are open. Two stone lions flank the entrance. The courtyard within is paved with cobblestones.

pages.caption: And went in to see the king.
pages.scene: Minnikin rides through the gates into the courtyard. Servants glance up from their work. The horse's hooves ring on stone.

pages.caption: The throne room was richly adorned with tapestries and light.
pages.scene: The throne room. Tapestries hang on the walls, depicting battles and hunts. Candles burn in iron sconces.

pages.caption: The king sat upon his throne in the great hall.
pages.scene: The king sits on a golden throne. He wears a crown and robes of deep purple. His beard is long and white.

pages.caption: Minnikin stood before the king, a small figure on the stone floor.
pages.scene: Minnikin stands before the throne. He is small beneath the high ceiling. The king looks down at him.

pages.caption: The king had a daughter who was very beautiful.
pages.scene: The king gestures beside him. On the arm of his throne stands a tiny figure, no larger than a doll. She is exquisitely beautiful.
pages.action: The king gestures toward the princess.

pages.caption: But she was so small that she could sit in the palm of your hand.
pages.scene: Close on the princess. She has flowing hair, delicate features, and eyes like jewels. She stands perfectly formed yet impossibly small.

pages.caption: She regarded Minnikin with curious eyes.
pages.scene: The princess turns her tiny head toward Minnikin. A small smile plays on her lips. She is aware of his gaze.

pages.caption: Will you marry my daughter?" said the king to Minnikin.
pages.scene: The king leans forward on his throne. His expression is expectant. He looks from Minnikin to the princess.

pages.caption: Yes, I will," said Minnikin.
pages.scene: Minnikin looks at the tiny princess, then at the king. His face is steady and resolute.

pages.caption: The king gave his daughter into Minnikin's care.
pages.scene: The king nods. He lifts the princess gently and places her in Minnikin's outstretched hands.
pages.action: The king places the princess in Minnikin's hands.

pages.caption: She sat in his hands as if she were made to be there.
pages.scene: The princess sits in Minnikin's cupped palms. She fits perfectly. Her tiny hands rest on his thumbs.

pages.caption: So they were married.
pages.scene: A wedding ceremony in the castle chapel. Minnikin and the princess stand before a priest. Candles burn on either side.

pages.caption: The priest spoke the words of blessing over them.
pages.scene: The priest blesses the couple. The princess stands on a pedestal beside Minnikin so they are the same height.
pages.action: The priest raises his hand in blessing.

pages.caption: They were bound together by the sacred vow.
pages.scene: Minnikin holds the princess's tiny hand in his. Their eyes meet. The chapel is hushed and golden with candlelight.

pages.caption: Minnikin took the little princess home to his mother.
pages.scene: Minnikin rides away from the castle on his horse. The princess rides with him, held safely against his chest.
pages.action: Minnikin rides the horse away from the castle.

pages.caption: They rode together across the open country.
pages.scene: The horse gallops across the countryside. Green hills roll on either side. The castle shrinks behind them.
pages.action: The horse gallops across the fields.

pages.caption: The cottage stood at the end of the road, as he had left it.
pages.scene: The cottage appears ahead. The chimney smoke rises into the evening sky. The mother stands at the door.

pages.caption: He brought the little princess to his mother.
pages.scene: Minnikin dismounts and carries the princess to the door. The mother leans close to see the tiny figure.
pages.action: Minnikin carries the princess to his mother.

pages.caption: His mother did not know what to think.
pages.scene: The mother peers at the princess in Minnikin's hands. She squints and tilts her head. Her brow furrows.

pages.caption: For the princess was so small.
pages.scene: The mother straightens up. She looks from the tiny princess to Minnikin and back again. Confusion and doubt fill her face.

pages.caption: But Minnikin loved her very much.
pages.scene: Minnikin holds the princess close to his chest. His expression is tender and protective. The princess gazes up at him.

pages.caption: On a high hill there stood a castle of black stone.
pages.scene: A distant hill. At its peak, a dark castle sits against gathering clouds. The stone is black and weathered.

pages.caption: Now there was a giant who lived in a castle on the top of a high hill.
pages.scene: Inside the dark castle, a giant sits on a throne of rough-hewn rock. His limbs are thick as tree trunks. His eyes are small and cruel.

pages.caption: He had heard of the little princess, and he wanted to marry her.
pages.scene: The giant leans forward on his throne. His jaw works as he thinks. Greed flickers in his eyes.

pages.caption: He rose from his throne, filled with desire.
pages.scene: The giant rises from his throne. His shadow falls across the floor like a storm cloud. He towers above his servants.

pages.caption: So he sent a message to Minnikin's mother.
pages.scene: The giant summons a messenger. The servant cowers before the giant's massive form. The giant speaks with a rumbling voice.

pages.caption: The messenger bore the giant's words to the cottage.
pages.scene: The messenger carries a scroll sealed with black wax. He hurries down the hill toward the valley below.
pages.action: The messenger runs down the hill.

pages.caption: A knock sounded at the cottage door.
pages.scene: The messenger arrives at the cottage door. He pounds on the wood. The sound echoes through the quiet evening.
pages.action: The messenger pounds on the door.

pages.caption: She received the scroll with trembling hands.
pages.scene: The mother opens the door. The messenger thrusts the scroll into her hands. His face is grim.
pages.action: The messenger hands the scroll to the mother.

pages.caption: Send me your son's wife, or I will eat you all up.
pages.scene: The mother breaks the seal and reads the scroll. Her face drains of color. The words are written in dark ink.

pages.caption: The threat hung in the air like a dark cloud.
pages.scene: The mother drops the scroll. Her hands shake. She looks toward the dark hills where the giant's castle stands.

pages.caption: The mother was very much afraid, for the giant was very strong.
pages.scene: The mother sits by the hearth. Her face is drawn with fear. The firelight dances on her worried eyes.

pages.caption: Fear gripped her heart.
pages.scene: The mother clasps her hands together. Her knuckles are white. She stares into the flames without seeing them.

pages.caption: Minnikin came home and found his mother in distress.
pages.scene: Minnikin enters the cottage. He sees his mother's distress and stops. The door hangs open behind him.

pages.caption: Do not be afraid, mother," said Minnikin.
pages.scene: Minnikin kneels beside his mother. He takes her trembling hands in his own. His eyes are calm.
pages.action: Minnikin kneels and takes his mother's hands.

pages.caption: I will go to the giant's castle and fight him.
pages.scene: Close on Minnikin's face. His jaw is set. His eyes burn with quiet courage. He is small but unafraid.

pages.caption: She feared for her son, yet she saw his resolve.
pages.scene: The mother looks at her son. Tears streak her cheeks. Pride and fear war in her expression.

pages.caption: At first light Minnikin prepared to ride.
pages.scene: Dawn breaks over the countryside. Minnikin leads his horse from the stable. Mist clings to the ground.
pages.action: Minnikin leads the horse from the stable.

pages.caption: So Minnikin rode away on his horse.
pages.scene: Minnikin mounts the horse. The mother stands at the cottage door, watching. Her silhouette is small against the frame.

pages.caption: His mother watched until he vanished from sight.
pages.scene: The horse gallops away from the cottage. The mother watches until they disappear over the first hill.

pages.caption: He rode toward the giant's castle.
pages.scene: The horse carries Minnikin across open moorland. Gorse and heather line the path. The sky is heavy with clouds.
pages.action: The horse gallops across the moor.

pages.caption: The sky darkened as he approached the giant's domain.
pages.scene: Storm clouds gather above the hill. Lightning flickers in the distance. The giant's castle is a black silhouette against the sky.

pages.caption: The path to the castle was steep and treacherous.
pages.scene: The horse climbs the steep hill. The path is rocky and narrow. Thorns claw at Minnikin's legs.

pages.caption: The gate of the giant's castle stood open.
pages.scene: The castle gate looms above. Its iron bars are rusted and twisted. The walls are cracked and covered in dark moss.

pages.caption: When he got there, the giant was not at home.
pages.scene: Minnikin rides through the gate into the courtyard. The ground is stained and uneven. No servant stirs.

pages.caption: The castle was silent and deserted.
pages.scene: The courtyard is empty. A well stands in the center, its rope frayed. Ravens perch on the battlements above.

pages.caption: The hall was dark, lit only by dying embers.
pages.scene: Inside the castle hall. A fire burns low in a massive hearth. Shadows crawl across the stone walls.

pages.caption: But the giant's wife was there, and she was a great big woman with three eyes.
pages.scene: A great chair sits by the fire. In it reclines a woman of enormous size. She has three eyes, one in the center of her forehead.

pages.caption: Her three eyes glowed in the firelight.
pages.scene: Close on the giant's wife. Her face is broad and hard. The third eye gleams like a dark jewel above the other two.

pages.caption: She fixed her gaze upon the intruder.
pages.scene: The giant's wife turns all three eyes toward the door. Minnikin stands in the entrance, small against the vast hall.
pages.action: The giant's wife turns to look.

pages.caption: She rose to her full, terrible height.
pages.scene: The giant's wife rises from her chair. She is immense, towering above Minnikin. Her shadow swallows the floor.

pages.caption: Where is my husband?" said she.
pages.scene: The giant's wife steps toward Minnikin. The floor trembles under her weight. Her three eyes narrow.

pages.caption: He would not show fear.
pages.scene: Minnikin does not step back. He stands firm, though the giant's wife blocks the only exit.

pages.caption: He is out catching men," said Minnikin.
pages.scene: Minnikin smirks. He speaks with a calm, steady voice despite the danger.

pages.caption: I have one eye more than you," said the giant's wife.
pages.scene: The giant's wife draws herself up. Her three eyes blaze. She points to her third eye.
pages.action: The giant's wife points to her third eye.

pages.caption: He knew the horse was his only chance.
pages.scene: Minnikin glances toward the door. His horse waits outside, restless and ready. He knows he must move quickly.

pages.caption: But I have a horse that can run faster than your husband," said Minnikin.
pages.scene: Minnikin speaks boldly, his chin raised. His small frame seems to grow with defiance.

pages.caption: Then the giant's wife was angry.
pages.scene: The giant's wife roars. Her three eyes bulge with fury. Her mouth opens wide, revealing teeth like jagged stones.
pages.action: The giant's wife roars in rage.

pages.caption: And she tried to catch Minnikin.
pages.scene: The giant's wife lunges at Minnikin. Her massive hands reach for him, fingers spread like talons.
pages.action: The giant's wife lunges toward Minnikin.

pages.caption: He dodged beneath her arms and fled.
pages.scene: Minnikin ducks under her grasping arms. He turns and runs for the door. His small feet pound the stone floor.

pages.caption: The horse awaited him at the gate.
pages.scene: The horse stands at the gate, rearing and snorting. Minnikin sprints toward it. The giant's wife crashes through the doorway behind him.
pages.action: Minnikin runs toward the horse; the giant's wife pursues.

pages.caption: But he jumped on his horse.
pages.scene: Minnikin leaps onto the horse. His foot finds the stirrup. He pulls himself up in one swift motion.

pages.caption: And rode away as fast as he could.
pages.scene: The horse bolts forward. Minnikin grips the reins. The wind tears at his clothes. The ground blurs beneath them.
pages.action: The horse gallops away at full speed.

pages.caption: The giant's wife ran after him.
pages.scene: The giant's wife bursts through the castle gate. She runs down the hill on her enormous legs. Her three eyes burn with fury.
pages.action: The giant's wife runs down the hill.

pages.caption: She pursued them across the open moor.
pages.scene: The horse carries Minnikin across the moor. The ground shakes with the giant's wife's footfalls behind them.
pages.action: The horse runs; the giant's wife chases.

pages.caption: But she could not catch him.
pages.scene: Minnikin looks back. The giant's wife is huge but slowing. Her long strides eat up the ground but the horse is faster.
pages.action: Minnikin looks back over his shoulder.

pages.caption: Her fury could not match the horse's speed.
pages.scene: The giant's wife stumbles on a rock. She falls to one knee. Her roar of frustration echoes across the hills.
pages.action: The giant's wife stumbles and falls.

pages.caption: She fell further and further behind.
pages.scene: The horse crests a hill. Minnikin looks back one last time. The giant's wife is a distant figure, growing smaller.

pages.caption: She could not catch him, and at last she stopped.
pages.scene: The giant's wife rises and shakes her fist. Her three eyes glare across the distance. But she does not follow further.
pages.action: The giant's wife shakes her fist.

pages.caption: He rode on, leaving the giant's domain behind.
pages.scene: Minnikin rides on. The landscape changes from barren moor to green forest. Birdsong returns to the air.
pages.action: The horse gallops into the forest.

pages.caption: Then Minnikin came to a forest of ancient trees.
pages.scene: A misty forest. Ancient trees with gnarled trunks stand like sentinels. Their branches twist overhead, filtering the light.

pages.caption: Mist clung to the ground like a silver veil.
pages.scene: The horse walks slowly through the mist. Moss hangs from the branches. The air is cool and still.
pages.action: The horse walks through the forest.

pages.caption: In a clearing there was a pond of clear water.
pages.scene: A clearing opens in the forest. In its center, a crystal pond reflects the sky. Three ducks swim upon its surface.

pages.caption: Three ducks swam upon the water, radiant and strange.
pages.scene: The three ducks glide across the pond. Their feathers shimmer with colors beyond nature: gold, blue, and silver.

pages.caption: They had been princesses, transformed into ducks.
pages.scene: The ducks turn their heads toward Minnikin. Their eyes are knowing and sad. They are not ordinary birds.

pages.caption: He walked toward the water where the ducks swam.
pages.scene: Minnikin dismounts and approaches the pond. The ducks do not fly away. They watch him with ancient eyes.

pages.caption: The first duck came to his hand.
pages.scene: Minnikin kneels at the pond's edge. He reaches out his hand. The first duck swims toward him without fear.
pages.action: Minnikin reaches toward the first duck.

pages.caption: Then Minnikin came to a castle where there were three princesses who had been turned into ducks.
pages.scene: Minnikin lifts the first duck from the water. It rests gently in his palms. Water drips from its shimmering feathers.
pages.action: Minnikin lifts the duck from the pond.

pages.caption: The other two ducks came to him as well.
pages.scene: Minnikin holds the first duck and turns to the other two. They swim closer, as if asking to be taken as well.
pages.action: The other two ducks swim closer.

pages.caption: He gathered all three ducks into his arms.
pages.scene: Minnikin cradles all three ducks. They nestle against his chest. The forest seems to brighten around them.

pages.caption: He carried them with gentle care.
pages.scene: Minnikin walks back to the horse with the three ducks. He places them carefully in his saddlebag, where they settle.
pages.action: Minnikin places the ducks in the saddlebag.

pages.caption: He took them home to his mother.
pages.scene: Minnikin rides through the forest toward home. The three ducks peer from the saddlebag, their eyes bright.
pages.action: Minnikin rides; the ducks watch from the bag.

pages.caption: The cottage stood as he had left it.
pages.scene: The cottage appears through the trees. The chimney smoke rises. The mother waits at the door as always.

pages.caption: He brought the three ducks into the cottage.
pages.scene: Minnikin dismounts at the door. He lifts the three ducks from the saddlebag. The mother watches with wide eyes.
pages.action: Minnikin lifts the ducks from the bag.

pages.caption: He set them down before the hearth.
pages.scene: Inside the cottage, Minnikin sets the three ducks down on the floor. They stand in a row, feathers glistening.
pages.action: Minnikin places the ducks on the floor.

pages.caption: The first duck became human again.
pages.scene: A soft golden light envelops the first duck. Its feathers dissolve like mist. A young woman emerges from the light.
pages.action: The first duck transforms into a princess.

pages.caption: She stood as a woman, restored to her true form.
pages.scene: The first princess stands in the cottage. She is young and beautiful, her hair cascading like water. She blinks in the light.

pages.caption: The second duck became human again.
pages.scene: A second glow surrounds the second duck. The feathers fall away like petals. Another princess appears.
pages.action: The second duck transforms into a princess.

pages.caption: She too was restored to her human form.
pages.scene: The second princess stands beside the first. She is taller, with dark hair and eyes like night. She smiles with relief.

pages.caption: The third duck became human again.
pages.scene: The third duck glows with the brightest light. All three princesses now stand in the cottage, radiant and alive.
pages.action: The third duck transforms into a princess.

pages.caption: They were together again, free from the enchantment.
pages.scene: The three princesses stand together. They embrace one another. Tears of joy run down their cheeks.

pages.caption: His mother could scarcely believe what she saw.
pages.scene: The mother watches from her chair. Her hand covers her mouth. Amazement fills her face.

pages.caption: Minnikin looked upon the most beautiful of the three princesses.
pages.scene: Minnikin looks at the three princesses. His gaze settles on the most beautiful. She meets his eyes with a warm smile.

pages.caption: Then Minnikin married the most beautiful of the three princesses.
pages.scene: Minnikin steps toward the most beautiful princess. He takes her hand gently. She does not pull away.

pages.caption: A feast was held to celebrate the marriage.
pages.scene: A wedding feast in the cottage. The table is laden with food. Minnikin and his bride sit at the head. The other two princesses sit beside them.

pages.caption: The mother's worry was replaced by joy.
pages.scene: The mother smiles at the head of the table. Her face is lit with happiness. The fear of the giant has passed.

pages.caption: They sat together, husband and wife.
pages.scene: Minnikin and his bride sit side by side. Their hands are intertwined. The firelight dances on their faces.

pages.caption: The cottage was filled with laughter.
pages.scene: The other two princesses laugh with the mother. The cottage is filled with warmth and the sound of voices.

pages.caption: They sat together by the warm hearth.
pages.scene: The feast ends. The five of them sit by the hearth. The fire crackles and pops. The night is quiet outside.

pages.caption: The world outside was calm and still.
pages.scene: Minnikin and his bride look out the window. The moon hangs over the rolling hills. The countryside is peaceful.

pages.caption: The giant's castle stood dark and abandoned on the hill.
pages.scene: The distant dark castle on the hill stands empty and silent. No light burns in its windows. The giant never returned.

pages.caption: Morning came to the cottage, bright and peaceful.
pages.scene: The cottage at dawn. Smoke rises from the chimney. Birds sing in the trees. The sun touches the thatched roof with gold.

pages.caption: They looked out together upon the wide world.
pages.scene: Minnikin stands at the door, looking out at the world. His bride stands beside him. The hills stretch green to the horizon.

pages.caption: They all lived happily ever after.
pages.scene: The mother brings breakfast to the table. All five sit together. The cottage is simple but filled with life.

pages.caption: And the story of Minnikin was told for all time.
pages.scene: The cottage from a distance. Smoke rises into a clear blue sky. The road runs past it, winding toward the horizon. The world is at peace.
